title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection & Pinning

transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Acme Head of AI), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Lindsay Brooks (Platform Eng), Ravi Shah (Security)

SUMMARY:
Quick sync to go over the model selection results from last week's evals, confirm which model variants we want pinned for the pilot, discuss fallback/rollback strategy, and confirm next steps (benchmarks + security docs).

TOPICS: model selection, quantization tradeoffs, pinning strategy, rollbacks/fallbacks, latency/cost numbers, security/VPC concerns.

TRANSCRIPT: 
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call - jordan here from redwood, maya and carlos with me. you good, elena?
[00:18] Elena Ruiz: yep, hi all. thanks, jordan. we got about 45 minutes so let's hit the high-level first then dig into the numbers.
[00:27] Maya Kapoor: quick agenda: review the eval spreadsheet, recommend pinning candidates, discuss how to handle rollbacks, and confirm benchmarks + security artifacts.
[00:40] Samir Patel: sounds good. i skimmed the spreadsheet, couple of questions on the cost column — can you walk through the assumptions?
[00:50] Jordan Lee: sure - the cost is based on a 1M token monthly projection, using the dedicated pricing model we discussed, plus an extra 20% for cache misses. note these are ballpark. maya, want to take the model perf bits?
[01:10] Maya Kapoor: yep. so we ran three catalog variants: rdx-3b-ptq (8-bit PTQ), rdx-3b-llmfp (LLM-FP quant), and rdx-6b-std. the 3b-ptq is the cheapest and lowest latency, the llmfp is a middle ground with slightly better quality on open-response prompts, and the 6b is highest quality but higher p95 latency and cost. many transcriptions mislabelled kernels but the net is the same.
[01:40] Elena Ruiz: our priority is clinical safety + precision on edge cases, but latency targeting is 400ms p95 or better for our triage product. if the 6b breaches that too often we can't use it.
[01:58] Carlos Mendez: noted. our p95 numbers on staging for rdx-3b-ptq are ~320ms end-to-end with our batching config (batch size 4, max len 512) - cost unit about $0.006/token estimate on the committed pool. rdx-6b-std was ~620ms p95 on the same infra.
[02:25] Lindsay Brooks: are those numbers with KV cache warmed or cold? caching changes p95 a lot.
[02:33] Maya Kapoor: those were with prefix cache warmed on common prompts, cold path adds ~80-120ms. so cold p95 for 3b-ptq was ~400ms.
[02:45] Samir Patel: quality — we saw a few hallucinations on medication names in the 3b-ptq runs; the llmfp variant reduced that but didn't eliminate. 6b was best.
[03:05] Elena Ruiz: that's expected... we can accept some tradeoff if we have a fallback to 6b for safety-critical prompts. what's the overhead if we route to 6b on fallback?
[03:18] Jordan Lee: fallback routing adds extra hop but we can do a synchronous fallback or async verification. synchronous fallback (route to 6b when trigger) means higher latency for that request but simpler correctness. we also support shadowing for offline verification.
[03:35] Ravi Shah: from security side we need audit logs of fallback events, and they must be retained for 90 days. is that supported?
[03:44] Maya Kapoor: yes — audit events for routing decisions are included in the console and can be shipped to your SIEM. we also have KMS integration for keys at rest. note: some transcription earlier mislabeled 'KMS' as 'kms-s' in the doc.
[04:00] Jordan Lee: so recommendation from redwood: pin rdx-3b-ptq as primary for the pilot with an automatic fallback to rdx-6b-std for flagged prompts, and a canary period where we log and review every fallback for first two weeks.
[04:18] Elena Ruiz: that seems reasonable. how do we define 'flagged prompts'? is that based on confidence score or a prompt-based heuristic?
[04:26] Carlos Mendez: we support a couple of strategies: token-level confidence, hallucination detectors, or simple heuristics like presence of medication entities with low model confidence. we can send a sample rule set.
[04:40] Samir Patel: we prefer deterministic heuristics initially — it's easier for auditing. e.g., any response where model reports <0.6 confidence on named-entity tokens triggers fallback.
[04:52] Maya Kapoor: we can implement that as a routing policy: rule -> route to 6b. note that confidence scoring is model-dependent and the calibration varies. you'll want to pin model versions to keep the score stable.
[05:08] Elena Ruiz: pinning — can you explain what that looks like in practice? i saw the draft pinning json you shared.
[05:16] Jordan Lee: sure. pinning is higher-level config stored in the deployment. sample fields: primary_model_id, primary_version, fallback_model_id, fallback_version, rollout_percent, canary_window. we'll send an exportable json you can commit to your infra repo.
[05:30] Lindsay Brooks: does pinning work across dedicated and private deployments the same way? we run some tests in our VPC.
[05:36] Maya Kapoor: yes it's consistent. API layer handles routing regardless of infra. for your VPC we provide a private control plane option and the same pinning config applies.
[05:45] Ravi Shah: important: we need SSO + RBAC for who can change pin configs, and an audit trail. is that supported?
[05:53] Jordan Lee: yes — SAML SSO, role-based permissions, and change history for pin config changes. we'll attach the section from our security doc.
[06:05] Samir Patel: on rollback — if we detect quality regressions after a rollout, what's the rollback latency? i.e., how quickly can we revert?
[06:14] Carlos Mendez: rollback is effectively immediate at the control plane level; changes propagate in ~30-120s depending on active connections. there's also an automatic fallback policy we can enable to revert to previous version if error rate exceeds threshold.
[06:30] Elena Ruiz: good. we need a chart of how many requests could be in-flight during a rollback and possible double-exec scenarios.
[06:38] Maya Kapoor: we'll add that to the benchmark doc. we do have a fail-open vs fail-closed option; for you we'd presumably fail-over to the fallback model rather than returning error.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: practical recommendation — for week 0 (canary) pin 100% to 3b-ptq for 90% of traffic, 10% to 6b shadow for offline checks. week 1 enable fallback on flagged prompts only. week 2 broad canary then full rollout.
[07:10] Samir Patel: one quick note — our compliance team will want an offline copy of the audit events for 1-year retention. is long-term export possible?
[07:20] Maya Kapoor: yes, we can stream logs to your S3 and lifecycle them with your bucket policy; there's a retention add-on if needed.
[07:28] Elena Ruiz: ok. about the pinning json — i want to see the exact version ids. last week the spreadsheet had some model ids mismatched to what we saw in demo.
[07:38] Jordan Lee: thanks for pointing that out. that was a typo — the id should be rdx-3b-ptq:v2026-03-29 and rdx-6b-std:v2026-04-02. we'll send corrected file.
[07:50] Lindsay Brooks: can you also include the exact kernel/runtime flags used for the latency numbers? that matters for reproducibility.
[07:58] Maya Kapoor: yes — kernel flags, batching config, and quantization knobs will be in the benchmark appendix. some earlier transcripts said 'kernel set' or 'kernal', those were typos in the doc.
[08:10] Samir Patel: about costs — you quoted $0.006/token — can you give p50/p95 token throughput as well so we can model autoscaling?
[08:20] Carlos Mendez: p50 throughput for 3b-ptq was ~1200 tokens/sec per pod under our test mix; p95 drops to ~420 tokens/sec. we'll provide the CSV.
[08:32] Elena Ruiz: regarding guarded prompts — we want a pre-filter that flags any prompt containing PHI patterns to route to a human review queue instead of fallback model. is that possible?
[08:42] Maya Kapoor: yes. you can add a pre-router lambda that checks for regex matches and re-routes. we can share a sample regex set.
[08:52] Ravi Shah: question: for private deployment do you support customer-managed HSM or only KMS? we need HSM for keys.
[09:00] Jordan Lee: private supports HSM integration (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM) — we'll include the architecture note. earlier doc copy had 'HSM' misspelled which caused confusion.
[09:10] Elena Ruiz: great. let's talk about concrete decisions — do you have a recommended pin config now?
[09:18] Maya Kapoor: yes. recommended pin JSON (verbatim excerpt): primary: rdx-3b-ptq:v2026-03-29, fallback: rdx-6b-std:v2026-04-02, fallback_policy: on_flag, rollout: 10% canary -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks, canary_review: manual. we'll send full file.
[09:40] Samir Patel: agree with that approach. can we add a secondary fallback (in case 6b is overloaded) to a cheaper but constrained model for degraded mode?
[09:52] Carlos Mendez: yes — multi-tier fallbacks are supported: primary -> fallback1 -> degraded. you can set rate-limits per tier.
[10:00] Lily (not present, placeholder): [inaudible] - -- // example of imperfect transcribed audio, removed for brevity
[10:12] Elena Ruiz: one more ask — can we run two test runs: one with full KV cache warm, one cold, to see worst-case latencies?
[10:20] Maya Kapoor: yes — we'll run those as part of the latency/cost microbenchmarks. we'll include configurations for both and the raw logs.
[10:30] Jordan Lee: ok, to summarize: redwood will send corrected pinning json, latency/cost csv, kernel flags, and security summary (SAML/RBAC/HSM + audit export). acme will provide failure prompts and provision staging network. target dates in action items.
[10:48] Elena Ruiz: good. any final questions?
[10:52] Samir Patel: small nit — can you include exemplar curl commands to exercise the pinned routing in staging? makes it easier for us to automate tests.
[11:00] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll include quickstart curl and a postman collection link.
[11:08] Lindsay Brooks: also share a sample terraform snippet if possible for the VPC peering config.
[11:14] Carlos Mendez: will do.
[11:18] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the canary for week of 2026-04-27.
[11:26] Elena Ruiz: thanks all. bye.

END NOTES:
- Links referenced: model pinning quickstart (https://redwood.ai/docs/model-pinning), benchmark csv (link to be shared), security summary (redwood.ai/security - will attach).
- Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (mis-typed product IDs, kernel/kernal, KMS spelled inconsistently).
